assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
scope is the validity and bias-control method for outcome backtests; model architecture and live deployment are delegated to sibling KBs
real, already-known historical outcomes are available for at least part of the population of interest
the scope finding 'medium-tier is the opportunity' (FP1) is treated as a falsifiable bet measured with a confidence interval, never as a premise
exclusions: predictive model architecture and feature engineering internals
live deployment, serving, and online monitoring

competency_questions.question: How is the backtest outcome defined and grounded in real known historical results?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OUTCOME_DEFINITION freezes the label rule and HISTORICAL_GROUND_TRUTH supplies real realized outcomes

competency_questions.question: What population does the backtest claim to generalize to, and how is the sample frame defined?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SAMPLING_FRAME defines the population and inclusion rule against the known-outcome ledger

competency_questions.question: How is survivorship bias detected and corrected so success rates are computed over entrants, not survivors?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SURVIVORSHIP_BIAS reconstructs the entry cohort within the declared frame

competency_questions.question: How is performance calibrated against the outcome base rate rather than raw accuracy?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BASE_RATE_CALIBRATION reports lift over the base rate after survivorship correction

competency_questions.question: How are hindsight bias and base-rate neglect prevented when choosing features and rules?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HINDSIGHT_BIAS blinds rule selection to outcomes; BASE_RATE_CALIBRATION removes base-rate neglect

competency_questions.question: How is single-origin / correlated evidence prevented from inflating confidence?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SINGLE_ORIGIN_EVIDENCE counts clusters not rows; HINDSIGHT_BIAS keeps selection outcome-blind

competency_questions.question: How is the data split temporally so no future information predicts the past?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TRAIN_TEST_SPLIT enforces a temporal cut; SINGLE_ORIGIN_EVIDENCE keeps clusters out of both folds

competency_questions.question: How is genuine out-of-sample generalization established rather than in-sample fit?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OUT_OF_SAMPLE evaluates the frozen model on untouched data after the TRAIN_TEST_SPLIT

competency_questions.question: How is out-of-sample performance estimated with its variability and without fold leakage?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CROSS_VALIDATION resamples with purging; LEAKAGE_AUDIT verifies no information crosses the split

competency_questions.question: How is overfitting to past virality and regime change controlled?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OVERFITTING_PAST_VIRALITY tracks in-to-out degradation; REGIME_CHANGE tests structural breaks

competency_questions.question: How is multiple testing across many strategies/features controlled, including via robustness checks?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MULTIPLE_TESTING_IN_BACKTEST corrects for trials; ROBUSTNESS_REPLICATION and LEAKAGE_AUDIT guard against artifacts

competency_questions.question: How is observed performance deflated for the number of trials and sample properties?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEFLATED_PERFORMANCE computes a fluke-adjusted metric from the trial count

competency_questions.question: How is every estimate reported with a confidence interval that drives the final verdict?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STATISTICAL_SIGNIFICANCE attaches CIs; VALIDITY_VERDICT carries them into the decision

competency_questions.question: How is 'medium-tier is the opportunity' (FP1) treated as a falsifiable bet measured with a CI rather than a premise?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MEDIUM_TIER_AS_FALSIFIABLE_BET tests FP1 out-of-sample with a CI that can refute; VALIDITY_VERDICT records the verdict

glossary.definition: a test that scores predictions against real, already-known historical outcomes rather than a simulated proxy
the unconditional prevalence of the outcome in the population, used as the no-skill reference for lift
over-representation of winners because failures, deletions, and dead accounts are absent from the record
the post-outcome tendency to view an event as having been predictable, inflating retrospective confidence
multiple cases drawn from one correlated source that are not independent observations
data untouched during fitting and selection, used as the only honest evidence of generalization
selecting a configuration that matches past data by chance after many trials, which fails to generalize
a performance metric adjusted for trials, sample length, and non-normality to estimate the probability it is not a fluke
a structural break after which past relationships no longer hold, violating stationarity
any path by which outcome-correlated or future information reaches the model at fit or selection time
a scope finding stated as a refutable hypothesis with an effect size and CI that can include the null or a negative

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for outcome-backtest validity and bias-control work units, informed by the backtest-overfitting, survivorship-bias, base-rate-neglect, hindsight-bias, and cross-validation literatures; no supplied dataset
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Bailey & Lopez de Prado 2014, 'The Deflated Sharpe Ratio: Correcting for Selection Bias, Backtest Overfitting and Non-Normality' (Journal of Portfolio Management); Brown, Goetzmann, Ibbotson & Ross 1992, 'Survivorship Bias in Performance Studies' (Review of Financial Studies); Kahneman & Tversky 1973, 'On the Psychology of Prediction' (base-rate neglect, Psychological Review); Tversky & Kahneman 1974, 'Judgment under Uncertainty: Heuristics and Biases' (Science); Fischhoff 1975, 'Hindsight is not equal to Foresight' (JEP: Human Perception and Performance); Arlot & Celisse 2010, 'A survey of cross-validation procedures for model selection' (Statistics Surveys)

nodes.definition: Define the binary or graded outcome the backtest scores against (e.g. 'went viral', 'beat threshold'), pin its measurement window, and freeze the labeling rule before any prediction is scored, so success is a fixed external fact rather than a movable target.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: outcome definition, threshold, or measurement window changes

pros.claim: A frozen, externally measurable outcome makes the backtest falsifiable and prevents post hoc relabeling of wins
pros.example: 'viral' fixed as >100k views within 14 days, set before scoring any item

cons.claim: A poorly chosen threshold can make almost everything or almost nothing a success, destroying discrimination
cons.example: a 1M-view bar labels 0.2% positive, leaving too few positives to estimate anything

failure_modes: outcome silently redefined after seeing results
window so long that later confounds contaminate the label
acceptance_tests: outcome label rule is written down and frozen before any case is scored
positive class has enough instances to estimate a rate

nodes.definition: Assemble the ledger of real, already-known historical results the backtest tests against: actual past items with their actual realized outcomes, with provenance and timestamps, distinguishing genuinely known outcomes from estimated or imputed ones.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new historical records added or outcome provenance corrected

pros.claim: Testing against real known results, not a simulated proxy, is the core of an outcome backtest and grounds every later claim
pros.example: each past post carries its true realized reach, not a modeled estimate

cons.claim: Historical ledgers are themselves selected and incomplete; what was recorded is not a random sample of what happened
cons.example: platform only retained metrics for posts that crossed a logging threshold

failure_modes: imputed outcomes treated as known truth
ledger silently filtered by an unrecorded inclusion rule
acceptance_tests: every scored case has a real realized outcome with provenance
imputed outcomes are flagged and excluded from primary scoring

nodes.definition: Specify the population the backtest claims to generalize to and the inclusion rule that admits a case into the sample, so the tested set is a defined, defensible slice of that population rather than an arbitrary convenience set.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: target population or inclusion rule changes

pros.claim: An explicit sampling frame turns 'works in general' into a checkable claim about a named population
pros.example: frame = all English short-form videos posted by accounts under 50k followers in 2024

cons.claim: Any frame narrows external validity; a result true on the frame need not hold on the population of interest
cons.example: trained on creator-economy posts but deployed on brand ads

failure_modes: frame conflated with the full population
convenience sample passed off as representative
acceptance_tests: the population and inclusion rule are written down and the frame-to-population gap is stated
revisit_triggers: systematic exclusion discovered in the frame

nodes.definition: Detect and correct survivorship bias: the systematic over-representation of winners because losers, deleted items, and dead accounts are absent from the record, which inflates apparent success rates and corrupts any model fit only on survivors.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: data source's retention/deletion policy or the dead-account recovery method changes

pros.claim: Reconstructing the full entry cohort (including failures) removes the upward bias that survivor-only data imposes
pros.example: recovering deleted/flopped posts from a pre-deletion crawl restores the true denominator

cons.claim: Lost cases are often unrecoverable, so the correction is itself an estimate with its own uncertainty
cons.example: deleted posts leave no trace, so the failure rate must be bounded, not measured

failure_modes: model trained only on surviving winners
success rate computed over survivors as if over entrants
acceptance_tests: the entry cohort is reconstructed or a defensible bound on the missing-failure mass is stated
success rates are reported over entrants, not survivors
revisit_triggers: a large block of deleted/dead cases is discovered

nodes.definition: Calibrate every claim against the outcome's base rate, not raw accuracy: report lift over the base rate, precision against the prevalence, and avoid the base-rate-neglect trap where a model that always predicts the majority class looks accurate while adding no information.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: outcome prevalence shifts or the calibration metric set changes

pros.claim: Scoring lift over the base rate exposes models that merely exploit prevalence and adds the information raw accuracy hides
pros.example: at a 3% viral base rate, 97% accuracy from always-predicting-no is worthless; lift makes that explicit

cons.claim: Base rates can be unstable or unknown for rare outcomes, making the calibration denominator itself uncertain
cons.example: a 0.5% base rate estimated from 200 cases has a wide CI on prevalence

failure_modes: raw accuracy reported against a skewed base rate
prevalence assumed constant when it drifts
acceptance_tests: every accuracy claim is paired with the base rate and a lift figure
a no-skill majority-class baseline is reported alongside the model
revisit_triggers: a new majority-class baseline beats the model on raw accuracy

nodes.definition: Control hindsight bias ('I knew it all along'): the tendency, after an outcome is known, to see it as having been predictable, which inflates retrospective confidence and contaminates any feature or rule chosen with knowledge of the outcome.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: feature-selection-vs-outcome separation protocol changes

pros.claim: Deriving features and rules without seeing the outcome breaks the 'knew-it-all-along' loop that makes the past look obvious
pros.example: analysts label predictive features on masked cases before outcomes are revealed

cons.claim: Full outcome blinding is hard to enforce when the same humans both know history and design the test
cons.example: an analyst already remembers which campaigns succeeded

failure_modes: rule chosen with knowledge of which cases won
retrospective confidence reported as if it were predictive
acceptance_tests: the predictive rule is fixed (ideally pre-registered) before outcomes are revealed to the rule's authors
revisit_triggers: a rule is found to have used outcome knowledge

nodes.definition: Establish point-in-time feature provenance: every predictor is reconstructed as it would have been known at each case's decision time, with documented source, lag, and as-of timestamp, so the feature set is constructed honestly before any leakage audit can confirm it.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a feature's source, lag, or as-of timing definition changes

pros.claim: Reconstructing each feature as-of the decision time builds look-ahead-free predictors by construction, before any audit
pros.example: follower count is read as of the post date, not the latest value

cons.claim: Point-in-time reconstruction needs historical snapshots that are often unavailable, forcing approximations
cons.example: only current follower counts survive, so the as-of value must be estimated

failure_modes: a feature uses the latest value instead of its as-of value
undocumented lag hides a look-ahead path
acceptance_tests: every predictor has a documented source, lag, and as-of timestamp consistent with the case decision time
revisit_triggers: a feature's source or lag changes
a snapshot gap forces an approximation

nodes.definition: Control single-origin (correlated-source) evidence: many cases drawn from one account, campaign, platform, or time slice are not independent observations, so they inflate apparent confidence and effective sample size far beyond the true independent information.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: clustering structure or independence assumption changes

pros.claim: Counting clusters, not rows, and using clustered standard errors keeps confidence honest when cases share an origin
pros.example: 30 hits from one viral creator count as ~1 independent signal, not 30

cons.claim: Defining the right clustering unit is judgment-laden; over-clustering wastes real information
cons.example: is the cluster the post, the account, the network, or the trend?

failure_modes: correlated cases treated as independent
effective sample size overstated by ignoring clustering
acceptance_tests: the clustering unit is declared and effective sample size / clustered standard errors are used
revisit_triggers: a dominant single source is found in the sample

nodes.definition: Partition the data into fitting and evaluation sets with a temporal cut, so the model is fit only on information available before each test case, preventing any use of future information to predict the past.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: split policy or temporal cut definition changes

pros.claim: A strict temporal split enforces that predictions use only past-available information, the minimum bar for an honest backtest
pros.example: a 2024-06-01 cut fits on pre-June data and tests on later items only

cons.claim: Temporal splits shrink the usable training set and can straddle a regime change that makes train and test incomparable
cons.example: the cut lands right before a platform algorithm change

failure_modes: future information leaks into the training fold
split point chosen to flatter the result
acceptance_tests: no test case uses any feature derived from information dated after that case
the temporal cut is fixed before scoring
revisit_triggers: a leak from future information is detected

nodes.definition: Run the genuine generalization test: evaluate the frozen model on data it never touched during fitting or selection, treating only out-of-sample performance as evidence of real predictive power rather than memorization.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: out-of-sample protocol or holdout boundary changes

pros.claim: Out-of-sample performance is the only honest evidence of generalization; in-sample fit is nearly always optimistic
pros.example: a model with 0.9 in-sample AUC but 0.55 out-of-sample is exposed as overfit

cons.claim: A single holdout can be lucky or unlucky; one out-of-sample number has its own sampling variance
cons.example: a small holdout gives a noisy point estimate that can mislead either way

failure_modes: holdout reused for tuning, silently turning it in-sample
reporting in-sample numbers as if out-of-sample
acceptance_tests: the reported headline metric comes only from data untouched during fit and selection
the in-sample-vs-out-of-sample gap is reported
revisit_triggers: the out-of-sample gap widens beyond tolerance

nodes.definition: Use resampling (k-fold, blocked, or purged time-series cross-validation) to estimate out-of-sample performance with its sampling variability, while respecting temporal order and avoiding leakage across folds.

excluded: leaky random shuffling of time series

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: resampling scheme or fold-leakage policy changes

pros.claim: Cross-validation yields a distribution of out-of-sample scores, exposing variance a single holdout hides
pros.example: purged k-fold gives a mean AUC with a CI rather than one fragile number

cons.claim: Naive k-fold on time series leaks information across folds and over-states performance
cons.example: random shuffling lets near-future leak into a fold's training set

failure_modes: random CV on temporally ordered data
overlapping windows leak label information across folds
acceptance_tests: folds respect temporal order with purging/embargo so no fold's training set sees its test horizon
revisit_triggers: a leakage path between folds is found

nodes.definition: Control overfitting to past virality: a model tuned to reproduce the specific past hits captures idiosyncratic noise of those events and fails to generalize, especially when many configurations were tried until one matched history.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: model-complexity or search-budget policy changes

pros.claim: Penalizing complexity and watching in-to-out degradation catches models that memorize specific past hits
pros.example: a 40-feature model that nails 2023 hits but collapses on 2024 is flagged as overfit

cons.claim: Aggressive regularization can underfit a genuine but subtle signal, trading false discovery for missed discovery
cons.example: shrinking away a real weak-but-stable predictor

failure_modes: model fit to the noise of specific viral events
past hits reproduced by capacity, not by signal
acceptance_tests: out-of-sample performance does not collapse relative to in-sample beyond a stated tolerance

nodes.definition: Control multiple testing in the backtest: when many strategies, features, or thresholds are evaluated, the best-looking one is selected by chance as much as by skill, so significance and performance must be adjusted for the number of trials.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: number of trials or multiple-comparison correction method changes

pros.claim: Counting trials and deflating the best result removes the selection bias of picking the winner from many candidates
pros.example: testing 100 thresholds, the best Sharpe is deflated for the 100 looks before it is believed

cons.claim: The true number of trials is often unknown (analysts try many things informally), so the correction is a lower bound
cons.example: undocumented manual experimentation makes the effective trial count larger than recorded

failure_modes: best-of-many reported as if it were a single pre-specified test
trial count under-counted, under-correcting significance
acceptance_tests: the number of configurations tried is recorded and the headline result is corrected for it
revisit_triggers: an undocumented search history is discovered

nodes.definition: Compute a deflated performance metric (e.g. the Deflated Sharpe Ratio) that adjusts the observed in-sample performance for the number of trials, the non-normality of returns, and the sample length, yielding the probability that the result is not a fluke.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: deflation model assumptions or trial-count input changes

pros.claim: A deflated metric converts a raw score into a fluke-adjusted probability of genuine skill, directly per Bailey & Lopez de Prado
pros.example: a raw Sharpe of 2.0 across 50 trials deflates to a modest probability of true skill

cons.claim: Deflation needs an estimate of the effective number of trials and return moments, which are themselves uncertain
cons.example: mis-specifying the trial count or skew/kurtosis biases the deflated estimate

failure_modes: raw metric believed without deflation
deflation fed a wrong trial count and over-credits the result
acceptance_tests: the reported performance is deflated for trials, sample length, and non-normality before any go/no-go decision
revisit_triggers: the effective trial-count input is revised

nodes.definition: Attach uncertainty to every backtest estimate: report confidence intervals (preferably from the clustered, deflated, resampled distribution) rather than point estimates, so a result is judged by its interval, not a single flattering number.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: interval method or confidence level changes

pros.claim: Reporting an interval makes the precision of the claim explicit and prevents over-reading a noisy point estimate
pros.example: lift = 1.4x with 95% CI [0.9x, 2.1x] tells a very different story than '1.4x'

cons.claim: Intervals assume a noise model; the wrong model (e.g. ignoring clustering) gives falsely tight bounds
cons.example: an iid bootstrap on clustered data yields a CI that is too narrow

failure_modes: point estimate reported without any interval
CI computed under an iid assumption on clustered data
acceptance_tests: every headline estimate is reported with a confidence interval built on the clustered, deflated distribution
revisit_triggers: a CI is found to ignore the clustering structure

nodes.definition: Treat the scope finding 'medium-tier is the opportunity' (scope FP1) as a falsifiable bet, not a premise: state it as a hypothesis with a directional effect, test it out-of-sample against the medium-tier subpopulation, and report the result as an effect size with a confidence interval that can include zero or a negative value.

included: effect size with CI that can refute
excluded: assuming FP1 is true a priori

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the medium-tier hypothesis definition or its tier boundary changes

pros.claim: Framing FP1 as a bet with a refutable CI prevents a hunch from hardening into an unexamined premise that drives strategy
pros.example: FP1 tested: medium-tier lift = 1.15x, 95% CI [0.95x, 1.38x] -> not yet established, do not bet on it

cons.claim: A medium-tier definition is itself a choice; a different tier boundary can flip the verdict, so the boundary must be pre-stated
cons.example: defining medium-tier as 10k-100k vs 5k-200k followers changes the estimated effect

failure_modes: FP1 assumed true and never tested
tier boundary tuned until FP1 looks confirmed
acceptance_tests: FP1 is written as a hypothesis with a pre-stated tier boundary and tested out-of-sample with a CI that could include zero or negative
revisit_triggers: FP1's tested CI crosses or excludes the null

nodes.definition: Account for regime change and non-stationarity: attention and platform dynamics shift over time, so a relationship that held in the past need not hold in the future; test for structural breaks and report the regime the result is valid within.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a structural break is detected or the regime window changes

pros.claim: Testing for structural breaks scopes the claim to the regime it was learned in and warns when past != future
pros.example: a 2022 model's edge vanishes after a 2023 ranking-algorithm change, flagged by a break test

cons.claim: Regimes are only visible in hindsight; a break detected late still leaves a window of invalid predictions
cons.example: the algorithm change is only identifiable months after it shifts the dynamics

failure_modes: a past relationship assumed stationary into the future
regime boundary ignored so cross-regime data are pooled
acceptance_tests: the result is labeled with the regime it is valid within and a structural-break test is run before extrapolating
revisit_triggers: the deployment regime diverges from the test regime

nodes.definition: Audit for information leakage end to end: any path by which outcome-correlated or future information reaches the model at fit or selection time (target leakage, look-ahead features, test contamination), which silently inflates every downstream metric.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: feature provenance or a new data join introduces a leakage path

pros.claim: A systematic leakage audit catches the single most common cause of unbelievably good backtests
pros.example: a feature computed using the full-period mean leaks the future into every row, caught by the audit

cons.claim: Leakage can hide in joins, derived features, and preprocessing fit on all data, so audits are never provably complete
cons.example: scaler fit on train+test together leaks test distribution into training

failure_modes: a feature that encodes the outcome or its future
preprocessing statistics fit on the full dataset
acceptance_tests: no feature uses information unavailable at the case's decision time and no preprocessing is fit across the split
revisit_triggers: a new feature or data join is added

nodes.definition: Test robustness and (where possible) replicate: vary thresholds, sub-periods, sources, and definitions to confirm the result is not an artifact of one arbitrary choice, and report whether the finding survives reasonable perturbations.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the perturbation set or replication source changes

pros.claim: A finding that survives threshold, period, and source perturbations is far more trustworthy than a single point result
pros.example: the medium-tier effect holds across three definitions and two independent creator cohorts

cons.claim: Perturbation testing is itself multiple testing; reporting only the configurations that survive re-introduces selection bias
cons.example: quietly dropping perturbations that broke the result

failure_modes: result reported from one lucky configuration
surviving-perturbations-only reported, hiding the failures
acceptance_tests: the result is shown to survive a pre-stated set of perturbations, and the perturbations that broke it are reported too

nodes.definition: Produce the final validity verdict: synthesize base-rate lift, bias controls, deflated out-of-sample performance, and robustness into a go / hold / no-go decision with its confidence interval, an explicit scope of validity, and the conditions that would falsify it.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the decision threshold or scope-of-validity policy changes

pros.claim: A verdict that carries its CI, scope, and falsifiers turns the backtest into an actionable, accountable decision rather than a number
pros.example: verdict: hold; medium-tier edge not yet established (CI crosses null); revisit after one more regime

cons.claim: A single synthesized verdict can over-compress the underlying uncertainty if the caveats are dropped downstream
cons.example: decision-makers read 'hold' and forget the CI that justified it

failure_modes: verdict issued without its scope or falsification conditions
caveats stripped when the verdict is communicated
acceptance_tests: the verdict states its confidence interval, scope of validity, and the conditions that would overturn it
revisit_triggers: a falsification condition is met in production

edges.why_related: undetected leakage manifests as apparent overfitting / too-good out-of-sample scores
correlated single-origin clusters must be kept within a single fold to avoid leakage across folds
a regime break shortens the effective stationary sample length used in deflation
the belief that medium-tier is the opportunity conflicts with calibrating against the medium-tier base rate, which may absorb the apparent effect
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.resolution_rule: FP1 is credited only as lift over the medium-tier base rate; if the medium-tier base rate already explains the apparent edge, treat FP1 as unconfirmed rather than a real opportunity

edges.why_related: limited real known outcomes create tension between maximizing the fitting sample and reserving an honest out-of-sample holdout
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.resolution_rule: spend known historical data on a strict untouched holdout even though it shrinks the fitting set; never recycle the holdout to recover sample size

edges.why_related: robustness perturbations improve trust but also multiply the number of trials, worsening false-discovery risk if uncounted
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.resolution_rule: pre-register the robustness perturbation set and count it in the trial budget; do not add perturbations until one survives and then report only that one

edges.why_related: fitting a model expressive enough to capture past virality conflicts with cross-validated generalization, which penalizes that expressiveness
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.resolution_rule: tune complexity using only the inner cross-validation folds and judge it on the outer untouched folds; never select complexity on the same data used to report performance

conflict_axes.name: raw_accuracy_vs_base_rate_lift
conflict_axes.description: Raw accuracy looks impressive against a skewed outcome but can encode pure base-rate exploitation; lift over the base rate is the informative but harsher metric.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always pair accuracy with the base rate and a no-skill baseline; judge on lift

conflict_axes.name: survivor_only_vs_full_cohort
conflict_axes.description: Survivor-only data is easy to obtain but biases success rates upward; reconstructing the full entry cohort is hard but honest.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: reconstruct entrants or bound the missing-failure mass before reporting any rate

conflict_axes.name: in_sample_fit_vs_out_of_sample_truth
conflict_axes.description: Maximizing in-sample fit reproduces history but overstates skill; out-of-sample performance is lower but is the only honest evidence.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: report only out-of-sample headline metrics and the in-to-out gap

conflict_axes.name: search_breadth_vs_false_discovery
conflict_axes.description: Trying many strategies raises the chance of finding a real edge but also the chance the best one is a fluke; correction shrinks the apparent winner.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: count every trial and deflate the best result for the number of looks

conflict_axes.name: sample_size_vs_honest_holdout
conflict_axes.description: Reserving an untouched holdout reduces the fitting sample, especially scarce when real known outcomes are limited.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: reserve the holdout first; use cross-validation to recover statistical efficiency without recycling it

conflict_axes.name: stationarity_assumption_vs_regime_awareness
conflict_axes.description: Pooling all history maximizes data but assumes stationarity; respecting regimes scopes the claim but shrinks usable data.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: test for structural breaks and label the regime the result is valid within

conflict_axes.name: clustered_evidence_vs_apparent_sample_size
conflict_axes.description: Treating correlated single-origin cases as independent inflates the effective sample; clustering is honest but reduces apparent power.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: count clusters not rows and use clustered standard errors

conflict_axes.name: premise_belief_vs_falsifiable_test
conflict_axes.description: Treating 'medium-tier is the opportunity' as a premise speeds strategy but risks building on an untested belief; testing it as a bet may refute it.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: state FP1 as a hypothesis with a pre-stated tier boundary and a CI that can include the null

conflict_axes.name: retrospective_confidence_vs_blinded_selection
conflict_axes.description: Designing the rule with knowledge of which cases won feels efficient but injects hindsight bias; outcome-blind selection is slower but valid.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: fix or pre-register the rule before outcomes are revealed to its authors

edge_cases.description: A model is fit only on surviving viral hits, so its success rate is computed over winners and looks far stronger than it is.
edge_cases.trigger: failures, deletions, and dead accounts are absent from the ledger
edge_cases.mitigation: reconstruct the entry cohort or bound the missing-failure mass; report rates over entrants

edge_cases.description: A classifier reports 97% accuracy on a 3% base-rate outcome while adding no information over always predicting the majority class.
edge_cases.trigger: raw accuracy reported against a highly skewed base rate
edge_cases.mitigation: report lift over the base rate and a no-skill majority-class baseline

edge_cases.description: Features and rules are chosen with knowledge of which past items went viral, so the past looks obviously predictable.
edge_cases.trigger: rule selection is not blinded to outcomes
edge_cases.mitigation: fix or pre-register the rule before outcomes are revealed to its authors

edge_cases.description: Thirty wins from a single creator are counted as thirty independent successes, inflating confidence many-fold.
edge_cases.trigger: correlated single-origin cases treated as iid
edge_cases.mitigation: count clusters not rows; use clustered standard errors and effective sample size

edge_cases.description: A preprocessing scaler is fit on train and test together, leaking the test distribution into training and inflating every metric.
edge_cases.trigger: preprocessing statistics fit across the train/test split
edge_cases.mitigation: fit all preprocessing inside the training fold only and audit feature provenance

edge_cases.description: K-fold cross-validation is run with random shuffling on a time series, letting near-future leak into each fold's training set.
edge_cases.trigger: random CV on temporally ordered data
edge_cases.mitigation: use purged/embargoed time-series cross-validation that respects temporal order

edge_cases.description: One hundred thresholds are tested and the best Sharpe is reported as if it were a single pre-specified hypothesis.
edge_cases.mitigation: record the trial count and deflate the headline result for the number of looks

edge_cases.description: A 2022 model's edge silently vanishes after a 2023 ranking-algorithm change, but it is extrapolated forward anyway.
edge_cases.trigger: a structural break is not tested before extrapolation
edge_cases.mitigation: run a structural-break test and label the regime the result is valid within

edge_cases.description: A raw Sharpe of 2.0 across fifty trials is believed without deflation, when the fluke-adjusted probability of skill is low.
edge_cases.trigger: raw performance metric reported without deflation
edge_cases.mitigation: compute a deflated metric adjusting for trials, sample length, and non-normality

edge_cases.description: The medium-tier-opportunity finding (FP1) is assumed true and drives strategy without ever being tested out-of-sample.
edge_cases.trigger: FP1 treated as a premise rather than a hypothesis
edge_cases.mitigation: state FP1 as a bet with a pre-stated tier boundary and test it with a CI that can include the null

edge_cases.description: Only the robustness perturbations that survived are reported, hiding the configurations that broke the result.
edge_cases.mitigation: pre-register the perturbation set, count it as trials, and report failures too

edge_cases.description: The final verdict is communicated as 'go' while the confidence interval that crossed the null is dropped downstream.
edge_cases.trigger: caveats and CI stripped from the verdict when communicated
edge_cases.mitigation: bind the CI, scope of validity, and falsification conditions to the verdict itself

workflow.description: Freeze the outcome label rule, threshold, and measurement window before scoring any case.
workflow.gate: label rule fixed and positive class adequately populated

workflow.description: Build the ledger of real realized outcomes with provenance, flagging imputed values.
workflow.gate: every scored case has a real provenanced outcome

workflow.description: Declare the population/inclusion frame and reconstruct or bound the missing failures.
workflow.gate: rates reported over entrants, not survivors

workflow.description: Estimate the base rate and report lift and a no-skill baseline alongside accuracy.
workflow.gate: every accuracy claim paired with base rate and lift

workflow.description: Fix/pre-register the rule outcome-blind and declare the clustering unit for evidence.
workflow.gate: rule fixed before outcomes revealed; clusters declared

workflow.description: Apply a temporal cut so no test case uses future information.
workflow.gate: no future information in any training fold

workflow.description: Score the frozen model only on untouched data and report the in-to-out gap.
workflow.gate: headline metric from untouched data only

workflow.description: Run purged/embargoed cross-validation and audit for leakage across folds and features.
workflow.gate: folds respect time and no leakage path remains

workflow.description: Count trials, track in-to-out degradation, and correct for multiple testing.
Compute the deflated metric adjusting for trials, sample length, and non-normality.
workflow.gate: performance deflated before any go decision

workflow.description: Attach clustered/deflated confidence intervals and confirm robustness across perturbations and regimes.
workflow.gate: every estimate has a CI; result survives pre-stated perturbations

workflow.description: Test FP1 as a falsifiable bet and issue a go/hold/no-go verdict with CI, scope, and falsifiers.
workflow.gate: verdict carries CI, scope of validity, and falsification conditions

priority_rationale: OUTCOME_DEFINITION/HISTORICAL_GROUND_TRUTH/SAMPLING_FRAME ground the test; the bias controls (survivorship, hindsight, single-origin) and base-rate calibration precede the temporal split; out-of-sample, cross-validation, overfitting and multiple-testing controls plus deflation establish honest performance; significance, the FP1 falsifiable bet, regime and robustness checks feed the final validity verdict.

dominance_rules.rule: OUTCOME_DEFINITION must be frozen before any case is scored
dominance_rules.rationale: a movable outcome lets wins be relabeled after the fact and destroys falsifiability
dominance_rules.trigger: scoring begins with an unfrozen outcome rule
dominance_rules.action: block scoring until the label rule and window are fixed

dominance_rules.rationale: a base rate computed over survivors is biased upward and corrupts every lift figure
dominance_rules.trigger: base rate computed before the entry cohort is reconstructed or bounded
dominance_rules.action: recompute rates over entrants before any calibration

dominance_rules.rule: BASE_RATE_CALIBRATION must accompany every raw-accuracy claim
dominance_rules.rationale: raw accuracy on a skewed outcome hides base-rate exploitation
dominance_rules.trigger: accuracy reported without a base rate and lift
dominance_rules.action: reject the report and require lift over a no-skill baseline

dominance_rules.rule: HINDSIGHT_BIAS blinding must fix the rule before outcomes are revealed to its authors
dominance_rules.rationale: outcome-aware rule selection injects creeping determinism
dominance_rules.trigger: a rule is chosen with knowledge of which cases won
dominance_rules.action: discard the rule and re-derive it outcome-blind or pre-registered

dominance_rules.rule: TRAIN_TEST_SPLIT and LEAKAGE_AUDIT must pass before OUT_OF_SAMPLE results are believed
dominance_rules.rationale: future information or leakage makes out-of-sample numbers fictitious
dominance_rules.trigger: an out-of-sample metric is reported before the leakage audit clears
dominance_rules.action: block the result until no future-information path remains

dominance_rules.rule: MULTIPLE_TESTING_IN_BACKTEST trial count must be applied before DEFLATED_PERFORMANCE is reported
dominance_rules.rationale: the best-of-many result is a fluke unless deflated for the number of looks
dominance_rules.trigger: a headline metric is reported without the trial count
dominance_rules.action: record trials and deflate before reporting

dominance_rules.rule: SINGLE_ORIGIN_EVIDENCE clustering must be reflected in STATISTICAL_SIGNIFICANCE intervals
dominance_rules.rationale: iid intervals on clustered data are falsely tight
dominance_rules.trigger: a CI is computed under iid on single-origin data
dominance_rules.action: recompute with clustered standard errors and effective sample size

dominance_rules.rule: MEDIUM_TIER_AS_FALSIFIABLE_BET must be tested out-of-sample before VALIDITY_VERDICT treats FP1 as established
dominance_rules.rationale: FP1 is a hypothesis, not a premise; an untested belief must not drive the verdict
dominance_rules.trigger: the verdict assumes FP1 is true without an out-of-sample test
dominance_rules.action: run the FP1 bet with a CI that can refute and gate the verdict on it

dominance_rules.rule: REGIME_CHANGE structural-break test must run before extrapolating a result forward
dominance_rules.rationale: a past edge that spans a regime break does not transfer to the future
dominance_rules.trigger: a result is extrapolated without a break test
dominance_rules.action: label the valid regime and block extrapolation across a detected break

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not score cases before freezing the outcome definition; relabeling later invalidates every earlier score
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rescoring the whole backtest after a post hoc outcome redefinition

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not compute base rates or fit models on survivor-only data; reconstructing the cohort afterward forces a full re-estimate
anti_rework_rules.prevents: redoing all rates and fits once missing failures are recovered

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not report raw accuracy without the base rate; adding calibration later means re-communicating every claim
anti_rework_rules.prevents: retracting and restating accuracy figures after base-rate exposure

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not select features or rules with outcome knowledge; de-biasing afterward requires re-deriving the rule from scratch
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rebuilding the predictive rule once hindsight contamination is found

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not reuse the out-of-sample holdout for tuning; once touched it must be replaced with fresh untouched data
anti_rework_rules.prevents: sourcing a new holdout and re-running evaluation after contamination

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not report best-of-many results without counting trials; recovering the true trial count later changes every significance claim
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-deflating and restating all results after the search history surfaces

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not treat FP1 (medium-tier opportunity) as a premise; if strategy is built on it and it fails the bet, the strategy must be unwound
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reversing strategy decisions that were built on an untested medium-tier belief

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not extrapolate across an untested regime boundary; a late-detected break forces re-scoping every forward claim
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-issuing forward verdicts after a structural break is found post hoc

iteration_protocol.trigger: a backtest result looks too good to be true (near-perfect out-of-sample)
iteration_protocol.action: run the LEAKAGE_AUDIT end to end and re-check the TRAIN_TEST_SPLIT for future-information paths

iteration_protocol.trigger: the success rate is suspiciously high for the outcome
iteration_protocol.action: reconstruct the entry cohort in SURVIVORSHIP_BIAS and recompute lift in BASE_RATE_CALIBRATION over entrants

iteration_protocol.trigger: many strategies or thresholds were tried before the reported one
iteration_protocol.action: count the trials in MULTIPLE_TESTING_IN_BACKTEST and recompute the deflated metric in DEFLATED_PERFORMANCE

iteration_protocol.trigger: the sample is dominated by a single account, campaign, or platform
iteration_protocol.action: re-declare the clustering unit in SINGLE_ORIGIN_EVIDENCE and widen the intervals in STATISTICAL_SIGNIFICANCE

iteration_protocol.trigger: a structural break or platform-algorithm change is detected
iteration_protocol.action: re-label the valid regime in REGIME_CHANGE and re-run ROBUSTNESS_REPLICATION across sub-periods

iteration_protocol.trigger: FP1 (medium-tier opportunity) is driving decisions without a test
iteration_protocol.action: convert FP1 into a falsifiable bet in MEDIUM_TIER_AS_FALSIFIABLE_BET and gate the VALIDITY_VERDICT on its CI

iteration_protocol.trigger: in-sample performance far exceeds out-of-sample performance
iteration_protocol.action: increase regularization or reduce capacity in OVERFITTING_PAST_VIRALITY and re-estimate via CROSS_VALIDATION

iteration_protocol.trigger: a falsification condition fires in production
iteration_protocol.action: reopen the VALIDITY_VERDICT and re-test against fresh OUT_OF_SAMPLE data in the new regime

required_checks: all edge ids unique EDGE_XXX format
all from/to in edges reference valid node ids
all competency_question_refs resolve to valid CQ ids
all evidence_refs resolve to valid source_registry ids
all priority_order entries are valid node ids with no duplicates
high_risk_nodes (risk_if_wrong>=0.80) have non-empty acceptance_tests and human_review_required=true
conflict edges have signed_tension<0 and resolution_rule present
observed_impact=0.0 for all nodes (no observed data)
19-24 nodes, 32-40 edges, 8-10 conflict_axes, 10-12 edge_cases, 9-12 workflow steps
post_formula_checks: all derived fields non-zero after compute run
